title: SZ-00B - Welcome, Logistics, and GM Role

sections.title: Player text
sections.body: This is a standalone one-shot at Mox. We are here to tell a complete story tonight, learn the game as we go, and make sure everyone has enough information to participate comfortably.

sections.title: Player bullets
items: Your GM is Kyle, he/him. Kyle has 15+ years running in-person and online TTRPGs.
GM style for Daggerheart: story-first, roleplay-friendly, and mechanics in service of the table's fun.
Kyle plays the world, keeps the rules moving, asks questions, and helps everyone get spotlight.
You play one character. Say what they try to do, ask questions, and make choices from their point of view.
We will confirm session length, end time, breaks, bathrooms, drinks, and any Mox house policies before we begin.
Phones are fine for reference or emergencies. Please keep attention at the table when another player has the spotlight.
This is a complete story tonight: Session Zero, opening job, rising trouble, final pressure, and a short closeout if time allows.

Gmnotes: Script: Welcome everyone by name if possible. Say: I'm Kyle, he/him, and you can call me Kyle. I've been running TTRPGs for 15+ years, both in person and online. For Daggerheart, my style is story-first and roleplay-friendly: the mechanics are here to support the table's fun and help us resolve risky moments, not to make you memorize a rulebook. I play the world, frame scenes, make rulings, and help everyone get time in the spotlight. You play one character and tell me what they try to do. Before we begin, let's confirm end time, breaks, bathrooms, drinks, phone expectations, and any Mox house policies. This card exists before safety and rules so strangers know what room they are in. Keep it practical. The table needs confidence, not a speech. Checklist: Introduce yourself as GM; Name/pronouns: Kyle, he/him; Mention 15+ years running in-person and online TTRPGs; State story-first, roleplay-friendly Daggerheart style; Confirm headcount, seats, names, and any latecomers; Confirm session length and target end time; Cover Mox house policies or ask staff if needed; Point out bathrooms, drinks, and table logistics; Set phone policy: reference and emergencies are fine, attention stays...

Gmreadaloud: I am Kyle, he/him, and you can call me Kyle. I have been running tabletop games for more than fifteen years, both in person and online. My Daggerheart style is story-first and roleplay-friendly. The mechanics are here to help us resolve risky moments and make the story more fun, not to make you memorize a rulebook. I play the world, frame scenes, make rulings, and help everyone get time in the spotlight. You play one character and tell me what they try to do. Before we begin, let's confirm end time, breaks, bathrooms, drinks, phone expectations, and any Mox house policies.

Gmchecklist: Introduce yourself as GM Name/pronouns: Kyle, he/him Mention 15+ years running in-person and online TTRPGs State story-first, roleplay-friendly Daggerheart style Confirm headcount, seats, names, and any latecomers Confirm session length and target end time Cover Mox house policies or ask staff if needed Point out bathrooms, drinks, and table logistics Set phone policy: reference and emergencies are fine, attention stays at the table State that tonight is a standalone complete story
Gmprivate: Ask May or Mox staff for current house policies before the event if they are not already posted.
Playertakeaway: Players know who Kyle is, how the table works, where logistics live, and that questions are welcome.
Storytakeaway: This is a complete one-shot, not a campaign pitch or open-ended planning meeting.
Mechanictakeaway: Establishes GM role vs. player role before any Daggerheart rules are introduced.

Takeawayhelp: Players know who Kyle is Players know Kyle's name, pronouns, experience, and GM style. This cue gives Kyle credibility and lowers pressure for beginners: story-forward, mechanics-assisted, and open to interruption. "I am Kyle, he/him. I have run tabletop games for more than fifteen years, and tonight my job is to help the table tell a strong story without making rules feel like homework." If someone asks how strict the rules will be: "I care about the rules when they help the scene. If a rule would slow us down, I will make a clear ruling and keep us moving."
